stem: What is a limitation of using head ultrasound for intracranial evaluation in infants?

options.text: It cannot be performed in the first month of life.
It requires the anterior fontanelle to be open.
It involves high doses of ionizing radiation.
It is more expensive than an MRI.

explanation: The skull bone blocks ultrasound waves, so an open 'window' like the fontanelle is necessary to see the brain.
rationale: Think about why this test becomes difficult or impossible to perform as a child gets older.

optionExplanations.A: Ultrasound is very effective in the newborn period when the fontanelles are at their widest.
optionExplanations.B: The skull bone blocks ultrasound waves, so an open 'window' like the fontanelle is necessary to see the brain.
optionExplanations.C: Ultrasound uses sound waves and is completely free of ionizing radiation, unlike CT scans.
optionExplanations.D: Ultrasound is generally one of the least expensive and most accessible imaging modalities.
